facts.raw_span: asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
involvement of the upper respiratory tract, causing palatal perforation and stridor, necessitating a tracheostomy a year ago
no history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring measuring 2 × 1 to 8 × 7 cm on the face, arm, and thighs
saddle nose deformity, perforation of the hard palate, and necrotic plaques on the ear with destruction of ear cartilage
cervical lymphadenopathy: multiple, nontender, discrete nodes, ranging from 1.5 to 2 cm without surface changes
anemia (hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL)
normal kidney function test
normal liver function test
infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)
pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species

concepts.why: The presence of pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, and parakeratosis in the skin biopsy, along with the characteristic black yeastlike colonies in the fungal skin culture, are diagnostic of Chromoblastomycosis.
The isolation of Exophiala spinifera species from the fungal skin culture, along with the presence of pigmented hyphae in the histopathology, suggests an Exophiala infection.
The presence of pigmented yeasts and hyphae in the skin biopsy, along with the characteristic clinical presentation, are consistent with Phaeohyphomycosis.
It explains the involvement of the upper respiratory tract and destruction of ear cartilage.

rationales.F01: Erythematous scaly plaques are common in chromoblastomycosis
rationales.F02: Upper respiratory tract involvement is more typical of Exophiala infection and Phaeohyphomycosis
rationales.F05: Saddle nose deformity and palatal perforation are characteristic of Exophiala infection and Phaeohyphomycosis
rationales.F10: Foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts are characteristic of chromoblastomycosis and Exophiala infection
rationales.F11: Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and dense dermal infiltrate are characteristic of chromoblastomycosis and Exophiala infection
rationales.F12: Fungal skin culture showing black yeastlike colonies is diagnostic of Exophiala infection

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species in the fungal skin culture and the histopathological findings of pigmented hyphae and foamy histiocytes support Exophiala infection as the most likely diagnosis.
